newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN chief hails arrest of Rwanda genocide suspects.
newsitem.headline: UN chief hails arrest of Rwanda genocide suspects.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan welcomed news of the arrest in Nairobi Friday of seven suspects in the 1994 genocide in Rwanda, congratulating those involved and thanking Kenya for its cooperation.

In a statement issued through a U.N. spokesman, he said the arrests, including those of former premier Jean Kambanda and former senior military commander Gratien Kabiligi, "demonstrate the determination of the international community to bring to justice those accused of perpetrating some of the worst crimes known to mankind."

Between 500,000 and a million Tutsis and moderate Hutus were killed by Hutu troops and militia in the 1994 ethnic slaughter in Rwanda. A U.N. war crimes tribunal was set up later that year to prosecute perpetrators.
Annan said justice amd peace were indivisible and that, "without justice, healing cannot begin".
"The secretary-general extends his congratulations to those involved in today's action, and his thanks to the government of Kenya for their indispensable cooperation.
"He hopes it will not be long before others indicted by the International Tribunals for Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia are also brough to justice," the statement added.
The seven suspects, who were picked up in an operation involving tribunal officials and Kenyan police, were flown to Arusha, Tanzania, the seat of the tribunal.
